{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVMWpgs8AAAABZYG_ZA", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4BnW-xzhC_eT0", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4BnW-x", "number": 33, "title": "Account for MSX opcode-fetch waits while preserving standalone Z80 timing", "body": "## Problem

Both MSX models currently use bare-Z80 instruction timing. `cpu.rs` explicitly excludes machine waits, and `Machine::step` forwards those counts to every clocked device. A NOP therefore consumes four T-states instead of five, allowing too many instructions per video frame and distorting software delays and device polling. Prefix-heavy code introduces further discrepancies. This is an implementation-level compatibility gap; no commercial-title failure was observed in this investigation.

## Expected outcome

MSX1/MSX2 execution includes one extra T-state per ordinary M1 opcode fetch, including prefix fetches and halted fetch cycles. Standalone zero-wait CPU behavior remains available. Returned cycles, `Cpu::tstates`, device advancement and frame budgeting use consistent elapsed time.

## Context

- Clean local HEAD and GitHub main match `94a5dc58f7d0252b70b71cdd0d14f2083fae73ec`. Inspect `crates/msx-core/src/cpu.rs`, `lib.rs`, existing CPU/hardware tests, Wasm frame exports and browser pacing. [Baseline source](https://github.com/takahirox/msx-rust/tree/94a5dc58f7d0252b70b71cdd0d14f2083fae73ec).
- Reproduction: execute an original NOP sequence through `Machine::step`; each instruction currently returns four cycles. Existing CPU tests intentionally assert bare timings and must retain their purpose.
- [openMSX Z80 timing definitions](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/openMSX/openMSX/master/src/cpu/Z80.hh) provide the MSX timing contract. Its [CPU implementation](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/openMSX/openMSX/master/src/cpu/CPUCore.cc) distinguishes indexed-CB operand reads and interrupt entry. These are upstream evidence, not newly measured hardware results; implement independently without copying source.
- The [Zilog manual, printed pages 12–14](https://www.zilog.com/docs/z80/um0080.pdf) distinguishes ordinary fetches, special interrupt acknowledgement and halted fetch cycles. Interrupt entry must not receive an automatic wait merely because R increments.
- Open Issues are empty. Earlier #3/#11 established CPU/MSX2 support; #31 and merged #32 added RAM banking. [PR #32 CI](https://github.com/takahirox/msx-rust/actions/runs/39952319767) actually reports 122 Rust and 84 browser tests passing. Those tests do not establish MSX fetch timing. Review is reported in the PR/documents; submitted reviews and discussion are empty. No tests were rerun here.
- Scope is fetch-wait accounting and its integration. Access-phase synchronization, VRAM contention, other CPU correctness gaps and device-specific timing corrections remain separate work. MSX databook archive/mirror access failed; accessible manufacturer/upstream alternatives support proceeding.

## Pre-merge acceptance

- [ ] Provide a minimal machine-specific wait policy with a zero-wait standalone default and one-wait MSX1/MSX2 behavior. Preserve it across Reset, model changes and firmware/cartridge transitions. Count actual fetch events independently of R values, instruction byte length and data reads.
- [ ] Add original timing vectors with explicit zero-wait/MSX expectations: NOP and HALT entry/idle 4/5; `LD A,n` 7/8; immediate IN/OUT 11/12; register CB rotate and NEG 8/10; `LD IX,nn` 14/16; indexed-CB BIT 20/22 and rotate 23/25; LDIR repeating/final iterations 21/23 and 16/18. Cover taken/untaken branches and repeated/ignored DD/FD prefixes, including `DD FD 00` at 12/15. Displacement and final indexed-CB opcode reads add no fetch wait.
- [ ] Retain interrupt-entry totals of 11 for NMI, 13 for MSX IM0 with FFh and IM1, and 19 for IM2 in both policies, documenting the reference basis. Cover EI delay, HALT exit and subsequent handler fetches. Preserve existing standalone interrupt-vector behavior.
- [ ] Cover `LD R,A`, `LD A,R`, refresh wrap/bit-7 preservation and bounded yielding for an address space filled with prefixes. Assert each step's returned cycles equal its `tstates` increment; prevent duplicate or missed waits.
- [ ] Add synthetic machine integration coverage for both generations showing corrected elapsed time reaches VDP/commands, PSG/SCC, FDC and MSX2 RTC. Include independent VDP/IRQ boundary, audio sample-count and FDC transfer-delay assertions. Preserve frame overshoot accounting, PAL/NTSC budgets and clock frequencies; do not compensate by scaling device clocks.
- [ ] Preserve existing video, audio, disk, SRAM, firmware, slots, Wasm/browser lifecycle and ownership/provenance behavior. Update timing documentation to distinguish standalone and MSX counts and remaining approximations. Use original fixtures and bundled lawful assets; proprietary software or human gameplay is unnecessary.
- [ ] Coordinator runs and reports README checks before merge: `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo test --workspace --locked`, `./scripts/build.sh`, `node scripts/check-dist.mjs`, and `npm test`, with documented dependency/browser setup as needed. Review the complete diff against this Issue and resolve blocking findings before merge. Report actual failures/skips accurately.

## Optional validation

Compare an original instruction/HALT/interrupt trace against openMSX before merge if available. This comparison was not performed here and is not required. Passing specification-based tests establishes this timing correction, not broad commercial-game playability.

## Required post-merge verification

None.
